clue.text: False jewels used in national emblems

parts.note: something false is a sham, a fake
rocks is slang for jewels, especially diamonds

explanation.surface: Fake gems have been set into a country's emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAMROCKS are the national emblem of Ireland, hence the plural 'emblems'.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leafed clover plant is the traditional symbol of Ireland.

clue.text: Some of this is allocated for rope making

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A portion of this is set aside for making rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The agave fibre is a classic material spun into cord and twine.

clue.text: It's always a good time for greetings

definitions.text: It's always a good time for greetings

parts.words: It's always a good time for greetings
parts.note: the part of the day that, in a standard greeting, is always preceded by the word good, as in a polite hello after lunch

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests any moment is right to say hello; cryptically it is the time of day always called 'good' in a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The salutation used between noon and evening always pairs this period of day with 'good'.

clue.text: Boisterous players get plastered

parts.note: boisterous play is rough
the players in a show are its cast

explanation.surface: Rowdy actors end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' looks like slang for drunk, but here it means coated with plaster; 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall finished with a coarse coat of lime and gravel is described with this word, meaning rendered with plaster.

clue.text: Canons negative about new authority

parts.note: the canons of a cathedral together form its chapter

indicators.note: about means the word for negative goes around the abbreviation for new

parts.note: adverse means unfavourable or negative

explanation.surface: Church clergy are opposed to a fresh source of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside ADVERSE to give ANDVERSE; the phrase is quoted to cite precise authority for a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Citing the exact book section and line of scripture gives precise backing, so the phrase stands for authoritative sourcing.

clue.text: Coach senses what players need for guidance

parts.note: a stagecoach, or stage, is a horse-drawn coach
a sense is a direction, as in the sense of rotation

explanation.surface: A trainer perceives what athletes need to steer them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' and 'players' suggest sport; the coach is a stagecoach and the players are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors follow the written instructions in a script telling them where to move and how to act.

clue.text: Bones sailors put iodine on

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Seamen treat their wounds with antiseptic iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the small ankle bones, a plural anatomical term.

clue.text: Fish coming from East End to Waterloo

indicators.note: the end of the word East is its final letter

parts.note: a Waterloo is a crushing defeat, a rout

explanation.surface: Someone travels across London from the East End to Waterloo station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' suggests the London district; read it as the last letter of 'East'.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Suggest a hike

definitions.meaning: to bring up a point or idea for discussion
an increase, especially in pay or prices

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to put forward a question; the other is an increase in salary.

clue.text: Composite picture of one kitten I'd let run wild

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: letting the letters run wild scatters them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drawing of a kitten that the speaker allowed to roam free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run wild' shuffles I, KITTEN and I'D into IDENTIKIT, a police likeness built from stock facial features.
explanation.definitionFit: A police likeness assembled from interchangeable drawings of facial features, as in an e-fit.

clue.text: Send back an essential like fruit

indicators.note: send back means all the pieces are written in reverse order

parts.note: a is the same article as an
a must is something essential
as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: Return a vital item such as fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send back' reverses the whole run of pieces, not just one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned citrus like a mandarin or tangerine.

clue.text: A poem is put inside cover for protection

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article a used before a vowel

indicators.note: put inside means the word is goes into the middle of the word for poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
taken as written

explanation.surface: A verse is slipped inside a jacket to keep it safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Using AN for 'A' is a standard crossword liberty, as both are the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: To coat a metal electrolytically with an oxide layer that resists corrosion.

clue.text: Tree on Lake Superior

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
arch means chief or principal, as in archbishop or arch-enemy

explanation.surface: A tree stands beside Lake Superior in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake Superior' looks like the Great Lake; split it into L and ARCH ('on' just places one after the other).
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous conifer that sheds its needles in winter.

clue.text: Medication available from reception

definitions.meaning: medical care given to a patient
the way someone is received or dealt with, as in harsh handling

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both medical care and the manner in which someone is handled.

clue.text: Got carried away in conversation with a girl

indicators.note: in conversation means the words are spoken, so they are matched by sound

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle, carried along
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone got over-excited while chatting with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conversation' says RODE, spoken, sounds like the start of the girl's name; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so a girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: Demolished sound point of view in quad, perhaps

indicators.note: sound here means the word is spoken and spelt by its pronunciation

parts.note: something demolished has been wrecked
an angle is a viewpoint or perspective

explanation.surface: A ruined, noisy perspective on a college courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' turns WRECKED into its spoken form RECT. A quad (quadrangle) is a four-sided figure, and the answer is one example, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided figure with right angles is one kind of quadrilateral.

clue.text: One may be required later to get in artist wearing loud suit?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
dressed in something means wearing it
a check is a bold squared pattern, typical of a loud suit

explanation.surface: To be admitted, an artist dons a garish suit.
explanation.walkthrough: A ticket or promise allowing a postponed event to be claimed at a later date; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher or promise to honour an offer at a future date after postponement.

clue.text: Accountant tacitly contrived putting up rates of change

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant

indicators.note: contrived means the letters are artificially rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A finance officer has quietly arranged to raise interest rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges TACITLY into TALYTIC. 'Rates of change' are reaction speeds, which a catalyst increases.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction, raising the speed at which substances transform.

clue.text: Mince and a chile for this dish?

definitions.text: Mince and a chile for this dish?

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so these letters are cut up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe asks whether minced meat and a chilli pepper go into this dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince' rearranges AND A CHILE; the whole clue also describes a Mexican rolled tortilla with a spicy filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling, often meat, and covered in chilli sauce.

clue.text: Study position for shot of lake

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: Someone studies where to stand to photograph a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Constance lies between Germany, Austria and Switzerland; 'for shot of' is link padding in the photographic picture.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the English name of the Bodensee, a large Alpine body of water.

clue.text: Discretion keeping one silent

indicators.note: keeping means the word for discretion holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: tact is discretion in dealing with people
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Being discreet means keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' places I inside TACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood or implied without being spoken, unspoken.

clue.text: Oath from a very loud girl opposed to it

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
Ida is a girl's name
v, versus, means against
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shouting young woman swears she is against it.
explanation.definitionFit: A written statement sworn to be true before a lawyer or magistrate.

clue.text: Fall out of box

definitions.meaning: to spar with the fists as a sport

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to quarrel; the other is to engage in a bout of fisticuffs.

clue.text: As eccentric as Seurat's style?

definitions.meaning: Seurat painted in pointillism, using many small spots of colour

explanation.walkthrough: Georges Seurat was the pointillist painter, whose pictures are built from tiny spots; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means mildly mad, and literally describes something covered in spots.

clue.text: Where animals shelter from lakeside winds

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake, set at the side of the next piece
airs are light breezes

explanation.surface: Wild creatures take cover from the breezes off a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: These are dens, the hideouts of wild beasts.

clue.text: Instrument from desert island turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert or betray them

explanation.surface: A musical instrument found upturned on an uninhabited island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a sandy waste; it is the verb, RAT. 'turned up' reverses RAT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-necked Indian lute with sympathetic strings.

clue.text: Name-dropping crook's a funny fellow

indicators.note: dropping means that letter is let fall out of the word

parts.note: a gangster is a crook; the apostrophe s is a link here

explanation.surface: A criminal who boasts of famous acquaintances turns out to be a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropping' looks like boasting of famous friends; it means drop N from GANGSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker who tells gags, a comedian.

clue.text: Old-fashioned shed is derelict

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
cast means shed, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: An outdated garden shed has fallen into ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derelict' looks like an adjective for the shed; it is the noun, a person abandoned by society.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict is a person rejected and abandoned by society.

clue.text: Record field

definitions.meaning: an item written in a register or diary
the competitors in a race or contest

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an item written in a log; the other is the full set of competitors entered in an event.

clue.text: Piece of cake and tea one tucked into, comfortably seated here

parts.note: a piece of cake means something easy

indicators.note: tucked into means the numeral is put inside the word for tea

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Enjoying cake and a cup of tea while sitting snugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating; it places I inside CHAR, giving CHAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded armchair is the place where one sits in comfort.
